We must eat the spiritual bread and the spiritual wine, the belief in Christ and God's promise to us to be saved. And he will live in us and we and Him if we do. Forever. Eternally. The Spirit inside us. We as the body of Christ.

These dark sayings troubled even His disciples, and as often as the case, Jesus takes the time to explain what He's saying to them so that they have better understanding.

Jesus says that it's the spirit that is quickened, and that the flash profits nothing, that this is spiritually meat and drink, not literal. That "*the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life."*

He's literally telling them that it's an allegory for a spiritual salvation, and yet some couldn't believe despite being called His disciples. Despite having some semblance of faith, but not unto belief and thus missing the point and the mark, and not getting saved.

teachings.title: No communion in John's gospel
teachings.summary: John, written so the unsaved may be saved, records no breaking of bread or wine at the last supper, so no such ceremony is needed for salvation.
teachings.text:
Another note on this chapter, John's account of the last supper. As we have said throughout the Gospel according to John, this is written specifically to the unsaved so that they may understand and come to salvation by faith. So it is important to recognize that there is no account of the breaking of bread and blessing of wine, which were symbols used to explain Jesus' coming trials and death in the other Gospel accounts.

If a ceremony of eating bread and drinking wine were necessary for salvation, it would be mentioned here. Of course if it were mentioned, it would contradict the entire message of God's grace giving us eternal life through belief on His Son found in every chapter.

teachings.title: Converting to a denomination is not soul winning
teachings.summary: Winning people to a denomination's traditions and works-based grace is not soul winning; only the gospel of grace through faith in Christ gives a sure hope.
teachings.text:
I don't know who needs to hear this, but convincing someone to convert to your particular denomination, with how based and trad their services are, their vain traditions, architecture and earthly treasures, political power or philosophies and theologies of man, is not giving the Gospel and getting people saved.

You're not a soul winning by convincing people to believe your denomination's false doctrines of subscription-based Grace doled out through works, and finding out later if you did enough to merit heaven. That's not the simplicity of Christ, that is not the blessed hope found in Him.

It is only through giving the gospel of grace by faith, In Christ alone unto eternal salvation, the good news as proclaimed throughout the New Testament.

*Sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:*

How do you say you have hope within you when you say to someone that maybe they were chosen, or maybe they'll do enough works, or maybe they'll stick with it till the end repenting of enough sins, and maybe they might have to go to mythical purgatory and suffer, because what Christ did wasn't sufficient for you.

That's not hope, and it certainly isn't meekness and it shows a lack of fear of God, adding to his word knowing the price that pays.

teachings.title: Pentecost tongues were real languages
teachings.summary: The Holy Ghost first indwelt believers when Christ breathed on them in John 20, and at Pentecost He filled them to preach the gospel in real foreign languages, not charismatic gibberish.
teachings.text:
Acts chapter 2 picks up now, 10 days after Jesus' ascension, the 120 disciples and Apostles gathered in church, waiting in Jerusalem as Jesus had instructed. As they waited, suddenly the great room they were in was filled with a rushing wind and flames of fire, filling those assembled with the Holy Ghost.

The traditional teaching of this chapter says that this is the first time the Holy Ghost is indwelling in believers, quickening their spirit the same way saved Christians experience today, calling upon the name of the Lord. It's often preached as "until Pentecost, no one had the indwelling of the Holy Ghost." The Bible says in the OT believers who called upon the name of the Lord and were saved by faith did not have the Holy Ghost permanently within them, but were often described as being filled with Him at times to do great feats, prophesy and preach, or be used in some way to the glory of God. I believe this is what's happening here, because in John 20:22 (which we just [read](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/2295)), where risen Christ appears to them on Easter Sunday, the scripture says:

*And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost.*

I believe this was when the Holy Ghost, the comforter and 3rd person of the triune Godhead, first indwelled in those who are quickened by faith, in God's grace.

I could be wrong but that's how it reads to me, otherwise John is contradicting Acts, impossible. Given the context of what happens next, I think my interpretation is correct.

Now, on the primary holy day of the feast of [Pentecost,](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/2367) believing, practicing Jews from all over the world were required to make pilgrimage to Jerusalem and the temple for the feast of first fruits of the harvest, and the blood free will sacrifices of purification (Exodus 23:16, 34:22, Leviticus 23:16, Numbers 28:26).

The Bible says that these Jews came from every nation, and lists many of the nations in example. And as the 120, filled with the Spirit come out to the crowd this gathered, they begin to preach the Gospel to all, in their own languages. This miracle of God is astounding, as these faithful God-fearing people hear the good news of Jesus Christ in their native tongue.

Not the satanic jibberish of the Charismatics and so-called Pentecostals, but clear understandable language of those assembled there.

Not the mistaken doctrine that the disciples spoke Hebrew or Aramaic or Greek, and those assembled heard it in their own languages, but if speaking to a Mede or Libyan or whatever land the pilgrims were from, they were able to communicate the Gospel to them. How do we know this? By the reaction of the Jews from Jerusalem, who mocked what they heard as unintelligible chatter as their being drunken.

This is when Peter gives a blistering sermon addressed specifically to those mocking, and an indictment of the Jews of Judea.

Peter says obviously they aren't drunken, being only 9 in the morning, but that it's fulfilled prophecy. He then quotes Joel regarding how in the last days the sons and daughters will prophesy, and uses that verse to then lead them the further prophecy of Joel of the second coming of Christ.

Peter is not simply defending their speaking in tongues, but like Jesus did repeatedly in His ministry, Peter is using scripture they should be familiar with to bring them the Gospel. He quotes Joel 3's warning of what the day of the Lord will look like, and indicating to the crowd that it is all coming true. Warning them that if they are seeing sons and daughters with signs and wonders, preaching the word, maybe they should take heed of what the rest of scripture says. That "*Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved."*

This is the Gospel.

He continues, making clear precisely who Jesus is, what He did, that He did it among them as they well know, and that despite their knowledge they killed Christ. Peter lays the blame for this squarely on the Jews in Jerusalem.

teachings.title: No real presence, only remembrance
teachings.summary: There is no sacrament in the Lord's supper; believers remember Christ and give thanks whenever they eat together, and transubstantiation and real presence are neither taught nor hinted at.
teachings.text:
BTW if I wasn't clear, there is no sacramental aspect to this, no Lord's supper as it were, it's the meals we have together with other believers we're to remember Jesus, with the breaking of the bread and the drinking of the juice of the vine, or anything else that we eat together.

The idea of a real presence, or the Hocus pocus of a transubstantiation, is neither implied nor even hinted at. When two or three are gathered together in his name Jesus is there. He's always present. Our taking the time to remember him and thank God for the food, and acknowledging Christ's sacrifice for us it's just something we should do when we gather together.

People turning Christianity into a weird cannibal cult are the worst

teachings.title: The spirit of the Lord's supper, not the flesh
teachings.summary: How often a church observes the Lord's supper matters less than the spirit of it, and treating the physical bread and wine as a source of grace, as Rome and her offshoots do, is eating damnation.
teachings.text:
How various NT churches decide to engage in a Lord's supper together is really not important, so much the spirit by which it is done. Some do it in honor of the day leading to His death burial and resurrection. Some do it weekly. Some do it every meal they have at church or at home. I tend towards that, at least in the blessing and remembrance.

What isn't good doctrine is placing more in the physical eating and drinking than the spiritual application. Or placing it as a source for grace and salvation. The Catholic version of this and the Protestant spin offs have at their heart the wrong motives spiritually, and so eat and drink damnation unto themselves.

As Jesus says in **John 6**, *It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.*

Those that heard and didn't understand this were offended and many disciples left from following Christ, because they took spiritual things literally, just as the Jews condemned Him for these "dark sayings."

teachings.title: Tongues, prophecy and the preserved English word
teachings.summary: Tongues were languages and prophecy is preaching scripture to understanding, so services in a dead language, back-to-the-Greek scholars and Ruckmanites all err, and God has preserved His word in English in the KJV needing no outside interpreter.
teachings.text:
Paul continues his teaching to the Corinthians on spiritual gifts, having put in place the doctrine that we shouldn't covet and envy those who have received talents to the edification of the church that differ from ours, that all in the body serve the same head, that head being Jesus and through Him, the Father. Then making the case that being charitable, the love for others that God expressed to us, and Christ demonstrated on the cross, then we've a better gift than even those the Holy Ghost bestowed on many in this time. Specifically the ability to speak and understand foreign tongues, or languages.

The Bible is clear that this is the meaning. Not the nonsense gibberish of the pentecostal heathen. No where in the Bible does the term "speaking in tongues" exist (unless you read one of the perverted modern versions that sow false doctrine with confusion so often).

This gift is rather the use of those who can interpret or prophesy scripture to those who speak another tongue.

Like the Apostles and disciples on Pentecost, who spoke the Gospel to those pilgrims from all over the world, in Jerusalem for the feast. They spoke to understanding, and it amazed the crowd and acted as a sign, bringing thousands to belief as they heard the word of God in their native language.

Prophecy in the Bible is the preaching of scripture, and bringing the relevance of the word of God to the people. It is giving the Gospel to the unbelieving. It is teaching the law. It is relevant preaching to the building up of the church. It is the advice of proverbs taught at a mother's knee. It is the exhorting of the pulpit to the flock.

And if any of this be done in a language none of the hearers understand, as Paul says in chapter 13, it is of *sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.*

This goes for false religion that gives entire services in a dead language. It is to no one's edification but the speaker.

This goes for the "You must return to the Hebrew! You must return to the Greek! God's word is impossible to understand in English!" nonsense of puffed up "scholars" who take pride in their private interpretation and sowing confusion among the people to show how learned they are.

This goes to the Ruckmanites who take the preservation of the Word in the KJV to be a further revelation that is more perfect than the Greek and Hebrew, which is nonsense.

Paul says that if you have a gift of knowing a language that can be used for interpretation to the person being reached with the Gospel then use it, but not to show off to the believers who cannot understand it, which seems the case in Corinth.

As Pentecost showed us, God's word is powerful in any language, and in every tongue God, who is not the author of confusion can make His word known.

Verse 26 he wonders how it is so many in Corinth are puffed up by claims of their own doctrines and revelations and psalms, and strange tongues, etc. They apparently were many among them who, in covetousness and pride were deceitfully inventing whole doctrines and aping gifts they did not have, or bragging about gifts they were given and wasting them.

As for tongues, today we have the inspired Word of God, preserved by the Spirit, in English in the KJV. And we should be grateful that we need no one to tell us it's lingual meaning, as every word and term is defined in itself. There is no need to appeal to a concordance or other work of an unsaved man to explain to us the plain meaning of His scripture.

teachings.title: All believers are saints
teachings.summary: Saint is the New Testament title for every believer, not a rank Rome bestows for works, and the peace announced at Christ's birth is peace between God and men through grace.
teachings.text:
Another point to make regarding the introduction, that Paul addresses to the saints and believers, terms which are interchangeable in the New Testament. All believers are saints. It's a title bestowed throughout to all who believe. It is not a select few whose Works were so good that they are honored here on Earth with the title. By making a church of man the arbiter, and basing it on works, the Catholic church has cheapened the term. I am a saint. If you believe you are a saint as well. Even if your backslidden, even if you need to turn from sins that are consuming your life. And as saints we should turn from sin, we should live a righteous life as possible. Live up to it.

Secondly Paul frequently writes that he prays for Grace from God to us the reader, and with that grace, peace.

The only piece we have with God is through his grace, and Christ Jesus. At the nativity the Angels announced peace on Earth. Goodwill towards men. This is a message from God to man, that he is granting them peace with Him, and goodwill through the birth of Jesus. The angel isn't saying that they'll be peace upon the Earth between men, but rather peace between God and men.

teachings.title: No chosen people but in Christ
teachings.summary: Paul refutes the idea that Jews are God's chosen and Gentile believers lesser, there is only the one dispensation of grace, and Rome's sin of presumption keeps people from assurance.
teachings.text:
Again the focus of these first 3 chapters is attacking the idea that Jews are God's "chosen people," and that Gentile believers are somehow less-than in their inheritance. Paul puts this false notion to bed, emphatically. We are the second born who received the full inheritance and blessing. The Jews having sold it in their fornication for the pottage of earthly things.

Dispensationalists rely on the appearance of the word 'dispensation' in these passages, to justify their wicked heresy, while the text of it destroys them. There is only the dispensation of grace. The change is to extend it to all men, through Jesus Christ regardless of lineage.

There is no limit to the atonement, but the free will to believe the Gospel by those that receive it, and *In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.*

This destroys the damnable "mortal sin of presumption" made by the Catholic Church to snare the unsuspecting into never coming to salvation, and never having that confidence, put in bondage to dead works of the law, and reliant on the RCC to save them in the end. Sending millions to Hell.

teachings.title: Sealed unto the day of redemption, against false churches
teachings.summary: Believers are sealed by the Spirit with eternal life, and churches teaching you can lose or must earn salvation, or that they are the body, are false churches that cannot save.
teachings.text:
Note the doctrines here, that unity of faith into the body, where Christ is the head. That we are sealed by the Spirit, given eternal life, testified by the new man within us, that we may know and have confidence in our trust in God. This is the promise of salvation.

Denominations that teach you can lose your salvation, that you must earn it, that only they can give it, that they are the head and the body, teaching the vanity of the mind and tossing their members to and fro with every changing wind of doctrine, rather than standing fast upon the unmoving rock of the Word...these false churches cannot save. They are the bondsmen, keeping people in chains.

teachings.title: John the Baptist and believer's baptism
teachings.summary: John baptized believers by immersion as the answer of a good conscience, not to wash away sin, and his hard preaching told the Pharisees that descent from Abraham would not save them.
teachings.text:
The prophet who comes before Christ. The voice crying out in the wilderness. Telling all men to turn towards God, that the Messiah is coming. John the Baptist.

Jesus cousin, raised by his righteous parents, bringing people to salvation and baptising believers, by immersion, in much water.

Baptism not being the putting away of sin, but the answer of a good conscience by those who have called upon the name of the Lord for forgiveness of sin and everlasting life. The same unbroken line of faith from John to modern, NT Christians. (Note it's not John the Catholic or John the Lutheran)

He eschews comfort. Eats ze bugs. And rips face with hard preaching. Matthew 3 captures a moment of John's style of fire-breathing, hellfire and damnation preaching, in this case against the Pharisees and Sadducees. The religious leaders of Judea, come down to be seen where the actions at. Maybe to be baptized to seem holy. But John calls them out.

*O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.*

Much as Jesus would later, as detailed in Matthew 7 and 23, he calls out these hypocrites, this generation of vipers, false preachers who bear bad fruit. Not souls won, ready to accept Christ. They bring forth no fruit, thistles. False prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

Then he goes after their reliance on being special boys, born from Abraham, saying God could make a rock a son of Abraham. That their being Jews isn't going to save them. (RIP Dispensationalism).

He tells these reprobate hypocrites that Jesus who's coming, will sort them like chafe from wheat, into the fire. Cut down their tree, throw it in the fire. Brimstone-throwing preaching. Amen!

And Jesus, our Lord comes, whose shoes we aren't worthy to unlatch. And he goes down into the water, and straightway rises up out of the water with the Holy Ghost upon Him. And the blessing of the Father is given to the Son. Amen.

teachings.title: Fruit of souls won, and false prophets who bear none
teachings.summary: Throughout the New Testament the work of believers is winning souls for God's increase, while false prophets with doctrines of works and philosophy cannot bring forth that fruit.
teachings.text:
Paul continues his greeting to the churches in Colosse, including a shout out to the early church in Laodicea, churches he himself didn't establish in person, as the Gospel has been preached throughout the world, faith to faith, to the Gentiles, beyond even Paul's direct ministry.

All believers, members of the body of which Jesus is the head, united in spirit, in the joy of peace with God through grace and faith, sharing the goal of bringing increase, the harvest of fruit of righteousness, winning souls to Christ with the Gospel of reconciliation. Bringing forth fruit meet for repentance. Turning those that heard and believe towards God.

We see in epistle after epistle, in the Acts of the apostles, in Jesus' own ministry, and His sending of disciples out, two by two into the highways and hedges. We see it in John the Baptist's preaching in the wilderness. It is faith shared and souls won. To God the increase.

The so called holy men, vipers chastised by John and Jesus Himself, Peter and Paul, were unable to bring forth this fruit, to lead believers to Christ.

Neither can false prophets, and yet they are here in Colosse as they were in Galatia, Ephesus, in the Judean wilderness, as Satan himself, trying to lead the churches astray, causing others to sin, and damning souls with their doctrines of works.

It's the same play as Satan in the desert with Christ. We see it today. They beguile us with enticing words, to *spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.*

teachings.title: Upon this rock: the confession of Christ
teachings.summary: The rock Christ builds His church on is the truth Peter confessed, that Jesus is the Christ the Son of God, not Peter himself, and believers are lively stones built on it.
teachings.text:
Next we see they've moved on, and having come to Philippi, Jesus is again teaching His Apostles, and begins asking "*Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?*"

The apostles say that the people say *He is John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets.* It is interesting that the popular consensus regarding Jesus was that he was first and foremost a hard preaching prophet. John the baptist, Elijah, and especially Jeremiah were known for their fire breathing preaching, condemning sin and wickedness of those around them.

Then Jesus asks, "*But whom say ye that I am*?" And Simon Peter, (*Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone*), answers, saying "*Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God."*

To which Jesus responds; "*Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven. And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.*"

Taken in context, we see that Jesus in confirming Peter's profession of faith, that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, that this truth revealed to Peter by God, and to all of us through His word and received by faith, is the rock upon which Jesus is building his church. His congregation of believers.

We see that Jesus originally calling him cephas or Peter, which translated means a stone, a chip of rock, is here paid off. A long setup punchline, used by Jesus to make a point regarding the gospel being **The Rock**, that the truth of Jesus being the long-awaited Christ is the cornerstone upon which the church is built. And we who believe, as Peter says in his Epistles, are as lively stones like him, making up the edification, the building up of the church, the congregation of which comes together on the day of the Lord.

We know that Jesus, upon his resurrection, had with him the keys to Hell and death. That rock, the truth of the Gospel, this spiritual bread, grants eternal life to those who believe. That the gospel itself is the key. That the truth of it is the rock.

And again these  things that are spiritually discerned, and twisted into perverse doctrines.

In the Catholic heresy, Peter becomes the rock, the church, an earthly institution built by men, the bread literal, and so literally flesh. The leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees added to the word, just as Christ warned.

teachings.title: The law is good if a man use it lawfully
teachings.summary: Paul warns against fables and genealogies but says God's law is good for the lawless and sinners, so it still needs enforcing today against libertarian Christians who take liberty for license.
teachings.text:
So, as we wade into the doctrines laid out here, we see that Timothy is charged with instructing those he finds called to the office of bishop, or pastor as we call it in modern times (terms that come from overseeing a flock of sheep), that they give no heed to fables and genealogies that lead to foolish questions, and don't edify the congregation. This is similarly given to Titus, avoiding Jewish fables and endless genealogies to instruct the future leaders of these churches.

At the time of this writing, many of the apocryphal books had been in circulation, non-inspired and many heretical concepts, being used by Jews and similarly creeping in to the new Christian churches.

The ramifications of rejecting the teachings of the pastoral epistles can still be felt today, with apostate false church of Rome, which uses unqualified men in unbiblical positions and uses the apocrypha, Jewish fables, to create doctrines. Not just the fables of the already existing books during Paul's day, such as using Maccabees to create the lie of purgatory,  but false gospels of Thomas and Andrew, for example, which they've adopted their Mary-worship from.

Of course we have the genealogies attempting to paint "seeds of Abraham" as special, continued in dispensationalist heresy today.

Paul continues to say that, in instruction of these leaders to also stress the importance of *charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned.* The gracious love for others that comes from having a good conscience before God, being blameless and regenerate in the faith of Christ. Unfeigned, sincere. While all saved have reconciliation with God regarding their sin, it is a spiritual maturity that brings one to this gracious and merciful charitable love for others.

There are some, Paul informs us, that having neglected this trait, and professing themselves wise, have become fools. Vain jangling. Just pontificating on the matters of the law, and works, and neglecting the faith, and forgiveness and grace. Many such cases, even today.

Paul does caution that the law of God *is good,* in itself, for its purpose, which he lays out here. His admonition is against the legalistic works-based false teachers, not the law itself, which we who are saved have liberty from, but that the law continues to serve as a schoolmaster, and is *for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine.* To bring them to the knowledge of the Gospel, or at the very least, to punish wrongdoing on earth and to keep an orderly society, understanding that the majority of people are not saved.

To many people, both believers and naturally, unbelievers, see no benefit or roles in God's law being used today. "That was for those times. Not for today." But, as we see from this list of sins, there is a clear need to maintain God's law regardless of what current year is.

Whoremongers and whores, who defile themselves with mankind, murderers, liars and every other thing that is contrary to good teaching from scripture. It's a broad list, and we understand why there remains a need to enforce these things.

There is an element of libertarian Christian that doesn't just reject the Levitical laws and carnal ordinances, done away with in Christ, but see no need to enforce the laws of God, written in our hearts and proclaimed from Adam on by God. They take their liberty for license to sin, and will not support the role of government and the law to protect people from evil and bring people to the understanding that there is sin and punishment, which is key to coming to repentance and accepting salvation.

teachings.title: I know whom I have believed
teachings.summary: Paul, in chains, urges Timothy not to be ashamed of the gospel, teaching that predestination is in Christ, not of individual believers, and resting in the assurance that God keeps what we commit to Him.
teachings.text:
The introduction to this letter to Timothy, which Paul is writing from Rome, under house arrest, chained to a centurion day and night. We learn that Timothy got saved following his grandmother and mother to Christ, and was given the gifts of the Holy Ghost by the laying on of hands by Paul, an Apostle indeed.

In his bonds, Paul shares that it is memories of things like Timothy's accepting of the Gospel that bring joy to him while in his predicament, and to encourage Timothy and others who may read this epistle to be of good cheer, hopeful in Christ and not ashamed of Paul's status.

*For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.*

He goes on to embolden Timothy, not to be ashamed of the Gospel, to lean on the power of the Holy Ghost upon him. To be a partaker of the persecution Paul suffers, willingly, because it is to the glory of God and the furtherance of the Gospel.

Paul says to Timothy that God has called them, *called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began,* *But is now made manifest by the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ*.

Note it is the predestination of Jesus Christ, not of the believer, that brings us to be used by God for His purpose, now that Christ was made manifest in Jesus, who abolished death and revealed immortality through the good news. The Gospel.

This is how predestination works. Foreknowledge by God, predestinated in Christ, fufifiled in our belief, conformed to His use.

*For the which cause I also suffer these things: nevertheless I am not ashamed: for I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day.*

Blessed assurance. We hold the ernest of His promise in our quickened spirit, the Holy Ghost indwelling within. Even in his persecution and humiliation, Paul knows the victory already won. He will not be ashamed for having placed his faith in the living God.

**Romans 10:11**
*For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed*.

Paul needs to write this encouraging word because of the betrayal of some in the faith, who having regarded his predicament, abandoned Paul. Not speaking out for him, and in fact turned away from the Apostle. Phygellus and Hermogenes are named in scripture, to their everlasting shame.

But, not being a downer, Paul also gives praise to Onesiphorus for seeking him out and refreshing him in Paul's afflictions. Mercy and honor from God for being unashamed of the faith during tribulation.

We should pray we can be like Paul, or at the very least Onesiphorus, when tribulations come.

teachings.title: Endure hardness as a good soldier of Christ
teachings.summary: Timothy is charged to endure as a soldier, athlete and husbandman for the elect's sake, who become elect by believing rather than by Calvinist choosing, and to rightly divide the word against cankerous false teachers.
teachings.text:
Paul continues his impassioned appeal to his young charge Timothy, written near the end of his life, from chains. Under house arrest in Rome. Unsure of his future but confident in his fate, Paul seeks to put his son in Christ firmly on the rock of the gospel, and in chapter 1 had recounted that many in Macedonia that he'd won to Christ had turned their backs on him in his tribulation, and turned from the truth of the gospel.

Paul charges Timothy to be stedfast in the faith that won him, unashamed of Christ and the promise of God. Holding fast to the scriptures.

He begs Timothy to be strong in the faith that Paul had won him by, with many witnesses, that is others who believed and were born again, those saved by the word, so as to be able to teach it to others.

To endure hardness like a solider, as he's been called by God to be. Not entangled with any other cause or cares, but the one he's been drafted to.

To strive for mastery, like an athlete. Earning crowns for his victories, without cheating, but with excellence.

A husbandman, enjoying the fruits of his labor, souls won to Christ.

He then impresses upon Timothy these doctrines that he feels are most important, beginning with the truth; *Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead.* For preaching this is what brought Paul to be in bonds. Scourged and stoned. Now facing the end of his race, he says he's endured all these things for the elects' sake. For the souls won by the same Gospel he's been persecuted for. That it was worth it all for their sake, that they may obtain salvation in Jesus Christ.

(Note that he is saying they believed the preaching to be elect, and that he endured that they may have believed. Not that they were going to no matter what. Not that they were picked to believe, but having believed, become elected to the promise. This is not calvinism, but how the truth of the good news and the light of the Holy Spirit works in men to bring them to repentance and towards faith in God. That we must endure tribulation to share, that all men might be saved.)

Paul continues. This is a faithful saying, that he charges Timothy to teach others;

*For if we be dead with him, we shall also live with him: If we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us: If we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself.*

He writes that the vain babblings and striving, arguments about the law and doctrines not of scripture serve no other purpose but to subvert those who hear them. To keep people from the faith and salvation. It continues the theme of his previous letter to Timothy, about instructing church leaders at Ephesus to be first and foremost good witnesses to the word that men might be saved. Here too, he is seeking to reinforce this idea, especially where there are those like Hymenaeus and Philetus, teaching false doctrines and damnable heresies such as the resurrection having already been past. (Hymenaeus is the same heretic who Paul said he had given over to Satan for his blasphemy in 1 Timothy 1:20)

Like Phygellus and Hermogenes, who ashamed of Paul's bonds, abandoned him and the calling, weakening the power of the Gospel for those who witnessed their shame and fear.

These false teachers and weak leaders, subverting and deserting, are like cankers. Their striving and arguments like sores that fester and eat away at the word, leading men to damnation.

Instead he charges Timothy to study to be approved by God rightly dividing the word that he may be able to stablish the faith of many, where these heretics overthrow the faith of some.

*Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.*

Again, God knows who are His, but he lets, allows, every one that calls upon the name of Christ be saved.

teachings.title: Unto every good work reprobate
teachings.summary: Titus 1:16 describes Catholic, Orthodox and Anglican clergy, works-based false salvationists, LDS and JW leaders and Calvinist lordshippers, who are rejected of God and given over to their own unrighteousness and whose mouths must be stopped by the word of God.
teachings.text:
*Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled. They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.*

Every ordained Catholic priest, cardinal and 'pope.' Every Orthodox monk and Anglican bishop. Every works-based false salvationist. Every cult leader of LDS or JW. Calvinist lordshiper 'reformed' viper, with their corrupt modern translations. All of them.

They are rejected of God and given over to their own unrighteousness. And over and over again scripture teaches us to be Biblical Fundamentalists, to cling to God's word, and to reject those who seek to turn others from the truth. Others who, with itching ears and mired in their own sins, can be turned from the truth by these vain talkers. Their mouths must be stopped, and it is by the word of God that we shut them up.

teachings.title: The seed groweth, he knoweth not how
teachings.summary: The kingdom grows like sown seed and a mustard tree, God not dictating which seed sprouts, a rebuke of Calvinism and a picture of believers branching out by leading others to Christ.
teachings.text:
*So is the kingdom of God.*

Jesus uses all these things of His own creation to make simple the ways of God to us.

And a man sows seed, which grows after its kind, blade, and ear and fruit. He doesn't make it grow, it just does, and when it is ripe for the harvest he brings in the bounty.

And so is the Kingdom of Heaven. The seed is the word, Jesus tells us, and it will *spring and grow up, he knoweth not how.* Meaning God, represented as the farmer doesn't dictate to the seed that it germinate, that it sprout, when it should flower and bud, that it bear fruit. Only that it will as it will, and in due season be ready for harvest.

Obviously God knows *how,* but the point is He doesn't determine which seed sprouts, or the nature of how it grows.

It's a rebuke of Calvinism, but it is meant to give us understanding of the Kingdom and our role in it. Both as the sowers and the sheaves. How Heaven grows.

*And he said, Whereunto shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it?*

We are privy to these lessons. We are not given the parable only, for those with ears to hear, but given their meaning. Nothing hid. And scripture gives us the meaning that we who believe may gain deeper understanding.

Heaven is like a mustard seed, tiny but that grows massive trees, with branches spanning out, each branching further. We are the branches sprung out from the seed. We can trace our lineage in terms of believers who led others to Christ, who led still others, who eventually were those who brought us to salvation. Like a family tree, stretching back to the seed that was sown.

 *For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ. For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body, whether we be Jews or Gentiles, whether we be bond or free; and have been all made to drink into one Spirit.*
*For the body is not one member, but many.* **(1 Corinthians 12)**

The Kingdom of Heaven is *like* this. And for our understanding all of creation exists.

*And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it.*
*But without a parable spake he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.*

teachings.title: Children of the devil are spiritual seed
teachings.summary: He rejects the serpent seed doctrine as damnable and teaches that the children of the devil are reprobates given over by God, a spiritual seed that does not reproduce but recruits.
teachings.text:
It should not have to be said that the perverted and disgusting false doctrine that Eve had relations with the serpent is from the pitts of Hell and those damned reprobates who promote it are to be rejected, utterly.

Yes, there are children of the devil. They are those who are reprobate, given up and given over by God. They are of their father, the devil. Sons of Belial. That synagogue of Satan. It isn't a physical seed, but a spiritual one, and they don't reproduce, the recruit though guile, trauma, abuse, and appeals to the flesh. And they seek to do his will, and are at enmity with God and with humanity. Murderers from the first.

teachings.title: The way of Cain, the first reprobate
teachings.summary: Jude warns against reprobates who teach the damnable heresy of works and turn liberty into lasciviousness, using Cain as the first reprobate and first works-based heretic.
teachings.text:
In the epistle of Jude, he writes of the common salvation, *that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints.*

*For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ....Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain...*

The way of Cain is the way of works, self-righteousness, wrath, giving way to sin, and stubbornness and stiff-necked willful refusal to accept the gift of common salvation, *denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ.*

Jude is warning against reprobates, who teach damnable heresy of works, and turning liberty into lasciviousness, using Cain as an example, the first reprobate. The first works-based heretic.

teachings.title: The wickedness of man, not bloodlines
teachings.summary: The flood shows evil comes from man's own heart, not from foreign bloodlines or hybrids, so all men of one blood have free will and need salvation by faith.
teachings.text:
The story of the flood as a judgment upon mankind is clear throughout that it is man's own wickedness that God is punishing. That within 8 generations, mankind had fallen so utterly that it had corrupted the earth itself. That only Noah had stayed faithful, God's Spirit striving with him, but not so that of man.

It is humanity that has fallen. It is man that is corrupt and wicked of heart. The same as it was in the beginning as it is today.

This is an important biblical doctrine to understand.

Many false doctrines place evil as something that is 'other,' foreign, introduced by bloodlines or genetics or ancestry. That salvation is only for a certain people, elect by nothing other than genes.

But we see in Genesis 6 that it is man's own wickedness that destroys us. That our flesh is what brings us to sin. That by faith in God, man can find grace and salvation.

This is extremely important and is a tangential doctrine to the concept of free will and individual soul liberty/damnation.

If man is irredeemable by genetics, then it is by a false calvinist god. If man, is saved by an inalienable quality bestowed by a creator, then he hasn't free will. If man is judged by other's sin, he hasn't the individual soul liberty to be saved by faith in Christ, being condemned by another's actions.

Since the time of Adam in the garden, blaming his sin on Eve and God for creating her, man seeks to find an excuse to justify themselves before the Lord in His judgment.

To push it off on the devil for offering temptation. To place it on the sins of another.

But God knows our heart, and says *the thoughts of* man's *heart was only evil continually.*

There is none righteous, no not one.

And this understanding is the basis for the faith in God for salvation. The knowledge that to walk with God, to strive with His Spirit requires His grace and His promise of salvation. Not of ourselves, but as a gift of God. That we are wicked and sinful creatures, deserving death and Hell, and in need of saving.

By placing the blame on external forces, even upon the demonic lineage of quasi-human chimeras, for example, we say "maybe it's not our fault God. After all, maybe it's not our fault."

But God *hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth.* He made nations and habitations and divisions of people, but we are all one blood, given to the same temptation of the flesh, sinful nature, with free will and the need for salvation.

teachings.title: Heresies Drawn from Revelation 4
teachings.summary: Revelation 4:1 is John alone in the spirit, not a pre-trib rapture, and the chapter gives no support to Catholic vain repetitions, soul sleep or gnosticism.
teachings.text:
Some additional **Revelation 4** notes, particularly on heresy.

Pre-trib rapture dispensationalists will use the taking up of John to Heaven to claim this is the secret rapture, that not only John but all the saved, are gathered at verse 1. They have to point to this event, because the following chapter, **Revelation 5**, begins the opening of the seals and the tribulation that follows. But **Revelation 4:1**-**2** says nothing about the gathering of the elect (we will see that it is immediately after the tribulation, when the sun and moon are darkened).

*After this I looked, and, behold, a door was opened in heaven: and the first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet talking with me; which said, Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter. And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne.*

This is not the bodily resurrection of the saved, glorified unto God and gathered on the day of redemption. It is John, alone and in the spirit. Pre-trib rapture is a foolish doctrine.

Another heresy justified out of **Revelation 4**, the vain and repetitive prayers offered by Catholics. Jesus tells us in **Matthew 6:7**; *But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.*

Many Catholics will point to the praise given "without ceasing" by the 4 seraphim, the creatures before the throne of the Lord as a nullifying text that contradicts Jesus' instruction to us on prayer, and so repetitive speed-muttering "Hail Mary's" and the occasional "Our Father" until they become a mush of words used as an incantation to their idols they worship kneeling before them, is ok. It's preposterous. We shall praise the Lord without ceasing but that's not vain repetitions, but giving honor and glory to Christ.  In prayer here, in this life, we should follow the model of conversational praise, gratitude and petition laid out by Jesus, in the manner described.

Another heresy is the idea that when we die bodily, that our soul sleeps or something, rather than being in the presence of the Lord as the Bible says in **2 Corinthians 5** that to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord, and we see that there are men, in Heaven, the 24 Elders for example. (They are not the only souls in Heaven as we will see moving forward in **Revelation**)

We can also dismiss the wicked heresy of gnosticism, that "matter is all evil," because we see, again, scripture has a different idea of creation, that God looked upon what He made and it was good. Here in **Revelation 4** we see it in the praise given by the elders; *for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created.*

The Lord God does not take pleasure in the wicked.

teachings.title: The False Prophet and the Image of the Beast
teachings.summary: The second beast is the false prophet of a one world religion who makes a speaking image of the Antichrist, so believers should flee idolatry now.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 13**
*11 And I beheld another beast coming up out of the earth; and he had two horns like a lamb, and he spake as a dragon.*

*12 And he exerciseth all the power of the first beast before him, and causeth the earth and them which dwell therein to worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed.*

*13 And he doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men,*

*14 And deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles which he had power to do in the sight of the beast; saying to them that dwell on the earth, that they should make an image to the beast, which had the wound by a sword, and did live.*

*15 And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed.*

A second beast arises, with the horns of a lamb but the voice of the dragon. This is the false prophet who will be given power by the first beast to make a one world religion that worships the antichrist.

We see in verse 8 that ALL who dwell upon the earth whose names are blotted out of the Book of Life will worship the first beast as a god. Another way of saying this is that those whose names are in the Book of Life, the saved, will not. This is the discernment of the Holy Spirit acting within us. The patience of the saints.

Like Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego who were tempted by Nebuchadnezzar to worship the idol he had decreed all men of Babylon to bow to and refused, willing to be placed in the fiery furnace, so too will the saved by tested.

The second beast, the false prophet who will be the pope of this new world order religion that's formed around its leader as god, will perform what appear to be miracles, calling down fire from heaven.

And he will set up an image of the antichrist to be worshiped. An idol. Beware any religion that allows the worship of idols, now, because they are a picture of this beast religion. Like the jab serving as a picture of the mark, which we are about to discuss, religions of Idolatry are meant to desensitize people over time into accepting this blasphemy. Flee Idolatry.

Not only will the false prophet set up this idol to be worshiped, but he will cause it to move and speak.

**Psalm 115**
*5 They have mouths, but they speak not: eyes have they, but they see not:*

*6 They have ears, but they hear not: noses have they, but they smell not:*

*7 They have hands, but they handle not: feet have they, but they walk not: neither speak they through their throat.*

*8 They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them.*

The Bible tells us again and again how the statues and graven and molten images are as dead and lifeless as the false gods they represent to the idolators. God mocking idolatry as vanity and superstition. And so here, in the holy place of God as the antichrist sits proclaiming himself as God, an image of him is built to be worshiped by the whole world, and in what will be seen as a miracle, the idol will move and speak as if it were alive.

Many consider this the abomination of desolation as spoken of by Daniel, and given us by Jesus as the sign that the Great Tribulation has begun, to be steadfast as His salvation is at hand.

teachings.title: The Everlasting Gospel Preached Even in Wrath
teachings.summary: The 144,000 likely minister during the wrath, and the angel with the everlasting gospel shows a God who offers grace to all, not the god of Calvin.
teachings.text:
Here in chapter 14, we are reintroduced to the 144,000 first described in the parallel passage of Revelation 7, and given added details of who they are and whence they came and the seal upon their heads.

These saints, we are told, come from the 12 tribes of Israel, 12,000 from each, who were believers having the testimony of Christ. Virgins, without guile. We know from chapter 7 they will be sent to Earth during the wrath, coming down from Heaven where they are seen here with Jesus. They are sealed, as we are told in chapter 14, with the name of the living God upon their foreheads. These were redeemed among men, the first fruits unto God and the Lamb, who is Christ.

Again, I believe they are sent to minister during the three and a half years of wrath to those who were not saved prior to the rapture. Those that hadn't taken the mark yet during that 75 days that follows the abomination of desolation and the establishment of the antichrist and his false prophet, until the Day of the Lord.

Remember too, that the two witnesses will be preaching during this time. They who were able to stop the rains and call fire down from Heaven.

(It's interesting to note that the antichrist's false prophet is given power to rain fire by Satan, and will be opposed to the witnesses during this time, much like Jannes and Jambres who withstood Moses in the court of Pharoah, or the prophets )

Even as the grapes of wrath are poured, God would that none perish but come to the saving knowledge of the truth.

John describes seeing an angel flying *in the midst of heaven, having the everlasting gospel to preach unto them that dwell on the earth, and to every nation, and kindred, and tongue, and people, Saying with a loud voice, Fear God, and give glory to him; for the hour of his judgment is come: and worship him that made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and the fountains of waters.*

This is not the god of Calvin. This is not a god selecting those to save and those to condemn. This is a God who so loved the world that even as He rains hail and sends locusts from Hell to torment those who would not repent, who worship the beast, He offers hope through grace to those who can still choose to have faith.

teachings.title: Come Boldly to the Throne of Grace
teachings.summary: Because Christ is a High Priest tempted like us, believers go boldly to God through Him alone, with no need of saints, Mary or sacraments.
teachings.text:
*Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession. For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.*

Having established that Jesus is God, Who created all things but was made by the will of the Father a little lower than the angels, made flesh to suffer and die for our sins, we can know that we have a High Priest, an advocate, who isn't some lofty god uncaring of our foibles and weakness, but Who at all points was tempted as we are, and through Whom we may boldly enter before God, His throne of grace, seeking mercy and help in our times of need. With the knowledge that God understands and loves us. We may enter boldly because we have such a High Priest in Jesus, He is the only mediator between God and man. There is no other name under Heaven by which we may be saved. There is no work by our own hands which can save us. There is no doubt of our salvation to those that believe. We enter into His rest by heeding His word and believing it.

And so we see, there is no calling on a "saint," or "Mary" to intercede, to bring us salvation, or any works, rites or sacraments that saves us from death and Hell. There is only faith in God's word and His perfect work, done from the beginning. The Lamb slain before the foundation of the world.

teachings.title: The Veil Done Away in Christ
teachings.summary: The old covenant had mediators and a veil, but in the new every believer is a priest and temple, so religions restoring priests and sacraments reject the better testament.
teachings.text:
Building on this, and to further cement the understanding that Jews (and all Catholics and Dispensationalist Zionists, many Prots included) are perishing and have not the understanding of scripture.

In the old covenant man was given a process, mediators between them and God. The carnal ordinances and Levitical priesthood, the tabernacle in the wilderness and the temple built by hands, all served as an intermediary between God and His people. The reading of the law given in synagogues. The sin offering and free will offering and every sacrifice, the religious ordinances, feast and days, all a picture towards Christ to come, and administered by the Mosaic system given in the Old Covenant. The veil between Moses and the people. The veil between the Holy of Holies and the people.

But the people were blinded and *unto this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament.*

This veil is only done away with in  Christ.

And the law which condemned, that glorious, perfect law of God, which served as a schoolmaster to bring to the people the knowledge of sin and their need for salvation. The law which as we saw in Hebrews 8 was perfect, but the people failed. And so a better testament is given us.

*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:*

And so there is no longer a priesthood, we are all preists.
No longer a temple, we are all each of us a temple.
No longer a human mediator, Jesus is our High Priest.
No longer a nation of the flesh, but a spiritual nation of believers looking forward to that better country.
No longer a vail between God and man, Jesus tore it forever.

And so the false religions that deny this better Testament and deny the truth of the new covenant, and who place temples and preists and sacraments and ceremony between man and God, and the burden of the law upon man's shoulders, all stems from the fact that the Gospel is foolishness to them that remain perishing. That the natural man receiveth not the things of God.

teachings.title: Baptism and the Lord's supper are pictures
teachings.summary: Baptism and the Lord's supper are the two New Testament ordinances, pictures of Christ that hold no saving power, and turning them or the sabbath into works for salvation is damnable heresy.
teachings.text:
Finishing this section, and the understanding of ordinances and their proper place in our faith, it is important to note that while the ordinances of the Old Testament were done away with in Christ, there are two new ordinances made to which we should adhere. Baptism and the common blessing and eating of bread and drink, communion, what we call the Lord's supper.

Just as the ordinances of the OT held no actual power to forgive sin or earn grace, but were a picture of the Christ to come, so too the ordinances we are told to keep are an image of Christ, a long shadow cast that we remember Him, and the faith we share as saved believers.

In baptism, the believer is immersed in water, dead, buried and risen in the manner reminiscent of Jesus. Going down into death symbolically, and rising up out of the water, born again.

The Lord's supper, likewise, where we are asked by Jesus to remember what He has done for us, the breaking of His body and the spilling of His blood that we may be saved. To recall this when we gather together in an assembly of believers to eat. Not just blessing the food in His name, but seeing the picture of His sacrifice in the breaking of bread and sharing of the wine (juice, not booze). "Do this in remembrance of Me."

This is the purpose of these ordinances, just as the numerous ordinances of the old covenant were.

But, like the Jews at the time of Jesus, the ordinance of the flesh representing the spiritual, become an idol unto themselves, and mistakenly transformed into a work of righteousness. A means of salvation. A means of obtaining grace, (which is an oxymoron).

Some heretical and judaized churches even place keeping of the sabbath as an ordinance, and a work required for salvation, despite the clear teaching that this was a picture, and done away with in the new covenant.

And just like the Pharisees, many have replaced ordinances made for man with requiring the man be made for the ordinance.

And just as the Pharisees' approach led to hypocrisy and their inability to produce fruit, men ripe for repentance, create with their false gospel proselytes twofold more the child of hell than themselves.

Damnable heresy.

teachings.title: Do we do all we can to heal the spiritually sick
teachings.summary: The sign gifts ceased with completed scripture and modern faith healers are grifters, but the Spirit is upon us to preach the gospel, heal the brokenhearted and free the captive, and most of us hardly try.
teachings.text:
Finishing out chapter 8 of Luke, we have in rapid succession Jesus healing the man containing a legion of spirits, sending them into a herd of swine that drove into the sea, the daughter of Jairus, who Jesus raises from the dead, and a woman with a blood disorder that, by faith only, touched the hem of Jesus' garment and was made whole as He made His way to see Juris's daughter.

Luke being a physician continuously shows us Jesus as healer. While on earth, Jesus takes compassion on those that suffer, and does what He can to ease it, in Jesus's case, the virtue of His holy being given to make the sick whole, the dead walk and the demons be cast out.

But it was His mission to heal the sinners spiritually by the promise of faith. To make us whole, forgiven of sin and reconciled with God.

But in everything, by grace and compassion, a charitable love, Jesus gave all.

We aren't Jesus. We are weak vessels for the new man inside us. We can grow in faith and effectiveness for being used by God, as we are called to be, and amazing things will happen in our lives, but we can't literally raise the dead. We can't heal chronic illness. We can't cast out demons. The gifts of the Holy Ghost were for a sign until the completion of scripture, that a people unfamiliar with the Word could be drawn to the truth of Christ.

But, do we do everything we can, giving all we have in our humble power to heal the sick, to set behind devils, to help the perishing escape death?

There are weird sects calling themselves "apostles" and claiming the powers of the Holy Spirit, speaking "tongues," laying hands in dramatic fashion to "heal." Even using the sweat of their garments to act as "prayer cloth" guaranteed to cure what ails, "with just a small token of a love donation...."

These vipers mimic the acts of the real Apostles, in a clown show grift, spouting gibberish and writhing on the ground as if it were them who were possessed by a demon. Claiming power that's not theirs.

But that's not what I mean.

Do we do everything we can, giving all we have in our humble power to heal the sick, to set behind devils, to help the perishing escape death?

Do we live up to that saying of Christ that sets the tone for His mission in **Luke 4**?

*The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, to preach the acceptable year of the Lord.*

The Spirit of the Lord is upon us. He has anointed us into His holy priesthood, the priesthood of believers given charge that we preach the Gospel to every creature. To the poor of spirit that they be made whole. To heal the brokenhearted by the hope we have in Christ.  To preach deliverance to those captive by sin and the cares of this world, in chains to trying to work their own righteousness by the law, and coming short, perish in despair.

Do we do all in our power to make the blind see? Spiritually, giving them the light that comes from the Lord, magnified in us, showing them the right and straight paths? Preaching the word that faith may come, and open their eyes to the truth?

Do we set at liberty those bruised by their iniquities, freeing them from the yoke of sin? The liberty we share in Christ?

Do we preach the acceptable year of the Lord, the Jubilee. The forgiveness of all debts as we are called home to be His people forever in a Kingdom not made of hands?

Do we do everything in our meager power to show compassion on the spiritually sick that they may be healed?

The best of us fall short.

Most of us don't really even try.

And we see how Jesus, who without sin despite being tempted in all ways like we are, studied the scriptures, committed them to heart as a boy, and in constant prayer, seeking to do God's will, loving others, doing whatever He could. And giving all, that those things be fulfilled in Him.

teachings.title: Upon this rock: Christ, not Peter
teachings.summary: The rock the church is built on is the truth that Jesus is the Christ, not Peter as Rome claims, and taking up the cross was a literal call for the apostles.
teachings.text:
Later on, Jesus brings up the rumors of Him going around to the Twelve, who had been journeying throughout the land, now returned. He asks who do the people say I am? They say, like Herod, people wonder if He is John, or a prophet returned. But when He asks them who they think He is, *Peter answering said, The Christ of God.*

Here in Luke, the narrative moves to Jesus' admonishment to keep that quiet that His fate be allowed to play out. In **John 16**, in scripture that is taken out of context by Roman Catholics to justify their false church, Jesus replies to Peter's profession of faith that He is the Christ by saying that truth is the rock upon which His church is built. Catholic tradition twists this to make Peter that rock, and claim their earthly church was founded that day on a man, rather than Jesus and His Heavenly assembly of those who know He is Christ and believe.

It is worth mentioning only in that if their version were true, it is odd that it's overlooked everywhere else in the Gospels, and in context, not even present in John.

But affirming He is the Christ, as eleven of the Twelve believe, He again prepares them, that He must suffer and die, and rise again. Betrayed and rejected. And warns of any follow Him, to be prepared to take up their own cross daily, and follow Him unto death. That if they deny Him to save their own lives, they will lose it, but those willing to be faithful unto death will live.

We draw a spiritual doctrine from this verse, inspiration to get up every day willing to sacrifice, follow His commandments, read the Bible, pray, etc. Taking up our cross. But here, Jesus means it literally, as well. They are going to face death for His sake. They will be tempted to deny Him. To be ashamed of the word. His Gospel. And Jesus wants them to understand if they don't truly have faith in Him they will falter, seek to save themselves and in doing so, lose out on the Kingdom, He will say He never knew them when He comes into His glory. "Lord, Lord..." and all.

Again, we take from this spiritual application, and pastors will preach on how this is a lesson for us in improving our Christian walk, and it indubitably is. It is something that has comforted and edified me, and still does. It's something I try to remind myself of, especially those days you wake up not really feeling it. Cares of the world, infirmities of the flesh. Inspired by Jesus calling us to take up our cross and follow Him.

But for us it's not sleeping in, or turning to the word instead of sin or remembering to pray. For His disciples, it was literal.

teachings.title: Pray directly to the Father: one mediator
teachings.summary: Jesus taught and lived the pattern of prayer: often, privately and earnestly to the Father in His name through the Spirit, with no intermediary like dead saints or a mediatrix.
teachings.text:
Good morning. Pray. Jesus not only taught us the pattern of prayer, the Lord's prayer given to His disciples as a format, a way to approach prayer to God, but He lived a prayerful life, with which we can seek to emulate, showing us the manner of prayer.

Often. Earnestly. Seeking God's will and the acceptance to do it. Alone. Privately. Early in the morning. All night if needed. On your knees. In tears and joy. Praising God in thanksgiving. Seeking forgiveness. Asking for favor, always in His will.

Not publicly and loudly to show how holy you are. When gathered with the assembly, making it short and sweet and to the point. Not in vain repetition as the heathens and pagans who worship at the feet of statues, icons and graven images, but in humble conversation, directly with God our Father. We are His children. We shall want for nothing that is in His will to provide. He knows our needs before we do, and the Holy Spirit aids is in this, our direct contact to God, who dwells within us as saved believers.

**Romans 8:26**
*Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.*

And so we pray to the Father, in the name of the Son, through the power of the Spirit. Boldly going before God in thanks, praise and supplication. Praying directly to God without a need for any other intermediary.

**1 Timothy 2:5**
*For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus*

Not praying to dead spirits, which is divination and necromancy, an abomination to God. Not praying through a "mediatrix;" Jesus didn't say "Our mother..."

We have directly from Christ the form and context, pattern and practice of how we must pray. So, pray.

teachings.title: Heaven and Hell are real: the rich man and Lazarus
teachings.summary: Jesus' parables are built on real things, so the rich man and Lazarus shows Heaven and Hell are real, while Abraham's bosom as a waiting compartment is a dispensationalist error.
teachings.text:
I would be remiss if I didn't address some of the contentions that come from this parable.

There are some who take this teaching of Jesus and draw conclusions from it for doctrine that amount to them attempting to fit their square pegs into round holes. Who are applying the logic of men to the things of God.

There are some who deny Heaven and Hell entirely and to them they will say that this parable shouldn't be used to justify the doctrines of Heaven and Hell being real, fixed places in the cosmos. And the destination of the dead be they saved or unsaved.

They take a general rule of thumb that is true and apply it here in a way that's foolish. We shouldn't draw doctrine from parables taken literally. We aren't literally having the faith of a mustard seed. We aren't literally sowing seeds upon the ground. We aren't literally sheep, the enemy's not literally wolves. We are supposed to see that creation serves as a way of understanding God's word, which is spirit and which is life.

But what they fail to understand is that every parable that Jesus tells is of something we can understand. Of something real. Of lamps and oil and weddings and servants, of lords and stewards. Sowing seeds and harvesting the fruit. Jesus consistently uses creation as the backbone of his parables so that man can relate to what he's saying and take from it. The spiritual application that He's providing. That's no different here. God is not the author of confusion, and Jesus doesn't make things up.

So even if this is simply a parable and not an actual retelling of events, it still uses as its basis, reality. Identifyable and understandable concepts. Death and the life thereafter, or condemnation to Hell which is burning and fire.

Another mistaken doctrine that stems from this is the idea that Abraham's bosom is a place and not a body part. That prior to Jesus crucifixion there was no Heaven and Hell but waiting areas, that Lazarus went to a paradise that is part of Hell. That Jews who were saved in the Old Testament, All of the Israelite saints, that when they die they went to Abraham's bosom rather than to Heaven where Abraham awaited.

This is often paired with dispensationalist heresies. It's foolishness and the other extreme of using parables for doctrine.

We can't say for certain that the Lazarus of this story is Jesus's friend from Bethany, the brother of Mary and Martha whom Jesus loved. But it's unusual for Jesus in a parable to use the specific name rather than a certain descriptor. It's not that important that we know this detail for sure. It's the spiritual application of the parable that matters. That there are some who see the richness of life as sumptuous living and worldly success. Who serve mammon rather than God. And their ability to believe, to come to saving faith is hampered by their pride and arrogance. Their hypocrisy and covetousness. They're placing the justification before men above being justified by God.

There is a Heaven and there is a Hell and there is more to this life than the things that we store up here on earth.

Don't allow your comfort or your wealth or your respect among your peers to confuse you regarding salvation. All have fallen short and failed to uphold God's law. And don't allow the low status of some to make you see them as less than. Don't be a respecter of persons.

teachings.title: As the lightning: no secret coming of Christ
teachings.summary: Christ's return will be seen by all like lightning, with the saints gathered as Noah and Lot were taken before destruction, so the pre-trib secret rapture is a deception.
teachings.text:
When should the Kingdom of God come?

Jesus, asked this question of the Pharisees, says that the kingdom isn't an earthly kingdom. It is within us to be part of it. It is spirit. It is in our hearts. We who are saved are of the Kingdom. Jesus taught His disciples that when we do good in the service of the Lord unto others, the Kingdom is nigh unto them. When a people reject the Gospel, Jesus said to shake off the dust, telling them that the Kingdom was nigh unto them.

We carry the Kingdom of God in our hearts and the key to its entrance in the truth of the gospel.  It sounds corny and sappy to modern ears, just as much as it did the scoffers and mockers of Christ's day. They expected an earthly kingdom led by an earthly king. They saw their religion as being about political power and breaking free of Roman oppression and the restoration of Judea. Their faith in wealth and man.

But Jesus Christ came to offer something greater.

But knowing the impatience of man, and the weight of the world on even the most devout, Jesus offers us the hope of His glorious return, the coming of His wrath, and the gathering of the elect in the resurrection and rapture.

Jesus teaching on n end times prophecy is most extensively given in **Matthew 24**, but Luke's telling has the fundamentals and added insight.

Jesus says as weary and impatient as we may be, don't be fooled. If someone comes claiming a secret return of Christ, not to believe them because Jesus will appear as the lightening that spans to all edges of the sky. Unmistakable. All will see His return.

The dispensationalist heresy of a pre-trib rapture relies on a secret coming of Christ, which sets men up for being fooled by the antichrist. Let no man deceive you.

Jesus return will be for the unbelieving like the days of Noah, where everyone went about their business, until Noah and his family were taken in to the ark as sudden destruction came up on the rest. The wrath of God poured out from Heaven.

The same with Sodom, where the wicked vexed just Lot with their filthy behavior, and the people there did what people do, right up to the day Lot and his family were spirited away, gathered by angels, and fire rained down destroying the wicked cities.

2 Peter 3:3-6
*Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, And saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation. For this they willingly are ignorant of, that by the word of God the heavens were of old, and the earth standing out of the water and in the water: Whereby the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished*

Jesus says, in that day of the Lord at His return, which will be manifest to all, we who are saved will be gathered, like birds of carrion to a corpse. Where Christ is in the clouds we will go to Him, caught up together. And woe to those who turn back. Who doubt. Who like Lot's wife turn to their old life and things. Who believed in vain and put the things of this world before the kingdom. Those seeking to save their life lose it.

Make sure you know where you stand.

teachings.title: Not imminent: the signs before His return
teachings.summary: The thief in the night is for the unprepared; Christ gave signs to watch, the seals and great tribulation, before His coming gathers the elect and the wrath begins, so imminence and pre-trib are deceptions.
teachings.text:
*And they asked him, saying, Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass?*

One quick point I would like to make is in regards to the false doctrine of Jesus imminent return. That he could come at any moment, right now.

Dispensationalists teach a pre-tribulation rapture wherein Christ comes to the believers as a thief in the night. That is not supported by scripture. The thief and the night is in reference to those caught unawares. Those who are not prepared for his coming. They won't recognize the signs of the times and won't be prepared to meet him.

But for believers we are given what to watch for. If you know what Jesus's disciples are asking here in verse 7, They say teach us what to look for. In Jesus compares his teaching to the fig tree. That you can tell the season and when to expect the fruit. He lays out all of these things that must come to pass before the end. Before his return and the day of redemption. He gives us this information that we be not deceived. And if you think about it, The idea that we cannot know when he's coming and that there won't be signs that we can observe, that he will come secretly, and rescue believers from tribulations of man, is a great deception.

Jesus here lays out the timing of things, the first four seals, The four horsemen. The Antichrist, wars on a global scale, famine and pestilence, megadeth. The affliction of the entire world by Satan and his forces.

Then, at the fifth seal we see a shift where Satan's attention is no longer on all of mankind, but specifically believers. This is the great tribulation. This is where we will suffer for his name's sake. And it is His coming in the clouds that saves us. He comes with great signs and wonders in heaven, the sun and moon darkening, coming with a shout and in full glory seen by every man. The day of the Lord. The Rapture.
